children: Turkey's government expects inflation to slow to 28.4% this year and to 21% in 2027 before dropping to single digits in 2029, according to an updated economic roadmap presented by Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz on Sunday.
The government maintained the programme's main framework, with the primary objective remaining to bring inflation to single-digit levels and ensure fiscal discipline.
Growth forecast to reach 4.2% in 2027, 4.6% in 2028, and 5.0% in 2029.
Budget deficit-to-GDP ratio seen at 3.5% in 2027.
Programme aims to increase national income to over $2.2 trillion and exports of goods and services to $450 billion by the end of the medium-term programme period.
Government projects 2.1 million additional jobs and an unemployment rate below 8% by end of 2029.
Regional tensions and their impact on energy and commodity markets are being closely monitored, with measures taken to limit the impact on the Turkish economy, Yilmaz said.
A strong downward trend in inflation has temporarily levelled off due to supply-side pressures created by Iran war impact
Direct and indirect effects of the war on inflation have been estimated at approximately 7 percentage points.
